feed.title: Carbon superhighway reimagines CO2 movement at scale
feed.summary: ExxonMobil is developing a "carbon superhighway" along the Gulf Coast to address the limitations of traditional point-to-point carbon capture and storage (CCS) models. This integrated network connects multiple CO2 emitters to various storage sites and customers, offering greater flexibility for captured CO2 to be directed to permanent storage, enhanced oil recovery, or industrial uses. The system is designed to expand easily as new projects are added, allowing for efficient and scalable CO2 management.

feed.title: SLB, Equinor to Upgrade Vessel Under Multi-Year Well Stimulation Deal
feed.summary: SLB and Equinor have signed a multi-year agreement to provide advanced reservoir stimulation services on the Norwegian Continental Shelf. The deal includes a significant upgrade of the MV Island Captain well stimulation vessel, which will be converted to a fully proppant-capable vessel with expanded storage and increased pumping capacity. This upgrade aims to support the development of tight offshore reservoirs and maximize recovery from future wells in the region.

feed.title: CoStar Says U.S. Office Inventory Shrunk by 7M Square Feet
feed.summary: CoStar Group forecasts that U.S. office vacancy will stabilize through 2026 before gradually declining, attributing this to a significant supply contraction, with office inventory shrinking by seven million square feet over the past year. This reduction is primarily due to historically low new deliveries and an increase in demolitions. Despite a downgrade in net absorption forecasts for 2026 and 2027, the ongoing supply contraction is expected to drive down the national office vacancy rate, albeit slowly, while acknowledging potential risks from productivity gains through AI.

feed.title: Cal-Maine denies any wrongdoing in egg price-fixing settleme...
feed.summary: Cal-Maine Foods Inc., the largest egg producer in the nation, has agreed to a $1.5 million settlement and will donate 30 million eggs to resolve antitrust claims regarding egg price manipulation. Despite the settlement, Cal-Maine denies any wrongdoing, attributing communications cited in the federal complaint to a single former employee and stating that the alleged actions did not impact egg prices. The settlement has faced criticism for its relatively small financial penalty compared to the companies' profits during the alleged scheme, and it has brought renewed attention to a stock sale by Cal-Maine's founding family shortly after the Justice Department's investigation began.

feed.title: Dream Finders’ $2.2B Beazer Deal Puts Mortgage Capture In Focus
feed.summary: Dream Finders Homes is acquiring Beazer Homes USA in a $2.2 billion all-cash deal, aiming to become the sixth-largest publicly traded U.S. homebuilder. This transaction highlights a growing trend of homebuilders leveraging in-house financial services to boost profitability and streamline the homebuying process.
